name: app.settings
title: App:Settings
description: The declaration to configure app settings.

payloadkeys.title: Allowed apps
payloadkeys.content: The dictionary of allowed app settings.

subkeys.title: Allowed apps
subkeys.content: If present, the device only shows or launches apps with bundle IDs in the array. Include the value `com.apple.webapp` to allow all webclips. This applies to App Store apps, marketplace apps, and locally installed apps (using Configurator, Xcode, and so forth).
String containing an identifier to match an app.

subkeys.title: Denied apps
subkeys.content:
If present, the device prevents showing or launching apps with bundle IDs in the
array. Include the value `com.apple.webapp` to restrict all webclips. This applies to
App Store apps, marketplace apps, and locally installed apps (using Configurator,
Xcode, and so forth).
> Note:
> Denying system apps may disable other functionality. For example, denying the App
Store app may prevent users from accepting the terms and conditions for the user-based
Volume Purchase Program (VPP).
String containing an identifier to match an app.

subkeys.title: Allowed binaries
subkeys.content: If present, the device only allows binaries that match the binary identifier properties to run. A binary only matches when all the binary identifiers match. The device always runs system critical processes. Use "codesign -dvvv <path_to_binary>" to show the information you need to generate these values.

subkeys.title: Binary identifier
subkeys.content: Dictionary containing one or more identifier fields to match a binary.

subkeys.title: Code directory hash
subkeys.content: The 40 character code signature code directory hash of the binary.

subkeys.title: Signing ID
subkeys.content: The code signature signing identifier of the binary.

subkeys.title: Team ID
subkeys.content: The code signature team identifier of the binary. Use the value "\*APPLE\*" instead of an empty string for Apple binaries with an empty team identifier.

subkeys.title: Path prefix
subkeys.content: The file system path prefix to match binaries.

subkeys.title: Signing state
subkeys.content: The code signing state to match binaries.

subkeys.title: Denied binaries
subkeys.content: If present, the device doesn't allow binaries that match the binary identifier properties to run. A binary only matches when all the binary identifiers match.

subkeys.title: Binary identifier
subkeys.content: Dictionary containing one or more identifier fields to match a binary.

subkeys.title: Code directory hash
subkeys.content: The 40 character code signature code directory hash of the binary.

subkeys.title: Signing ID
subkeys.content: The code signature signing identifier of the binary.

subkeys.title: Team ID
subkeys.content: The code signature team identifier of the binary. Use the value "\*APPLE\*" instead of an empty string for Apple binaries with an empty team identifier.

subkeys.title: Path prefix
subkeys.content: The file system path prefix to match binaries.

subkeys.title: Signing state
subkeys.content: The code signing state to match binaries.

subkeys.title: Always allow managed apps
subkeys.content: If `true`, the device implicitly includes managed apps in the effective allow list when `AllowedBinaries` is present.

subkeys.title: App privacy permission defaults
subkeys.content:
The dictionary of app privacy permission defaults. Each key in the dictionary is an app identifier. The dictionary values represent the permission defaults that the device applies for each matching app.

In iOS, the app identifier is a bundle ID, for example, "com.example.app".

In macOS, the app identifier is a composed identifier. The format of the composed identifier is "Bundle-ID {Designated-Requirement}". "Bundle-ID" is the bundle identifier string of the app. "Designated-Requirement" is the designated requirement string the device uses to match the code signature of the app. For example, "com.example.app {anchor apple generic}". The device only applies defaults for an app if its code signature matches the composed identifier.
The dictionary that defines the app privacy permission defaults. Each key is an app identifier.

subkeys.title: Organization justification
subkeys.content: Text you provide that clearly explains to the user the reason why the organization requires these app permission defaults. The device includes this text in the permission consent prompt it displays when it launches the app.

subkeys.title: Accessibility permission
subkeys.content:
Controls whether an app privacy permission default is set.
* `None`: No app privacy permission default is set for use of accessibility.
* `Allow`: The app privacy permission default is set to allow use of accessibility.

subkeys.title: Bluetooth permission
subkeys.content:
Controls whether an app privacy permission default is set.
* `None`: No app privacy permission default is set for use of Bluetooth.
* `Allow`: The app privacy permission default is set to allow use of Bluetooth.

subkeys.title: Camera permission
subkeys.content:
Controls whether an app privacy permission default is set.
* `None`: No app privacy permission default is set for use of the camera.
* `Allow`: The app privacy permission default is set to allow use of the camera.

subkeys.title: Dictation permission
subkeys.content:
Controls whether an app privacy permission default is set.
* `None`: No app privacy permission default is set for use of dictation.
* `Allow`: The app privacy permission default is set to allow use of dictation.

subkeys.title: Local network permission
subkeys.content:
Controls whether an app privacy permission default is set.
* `None`: No app privacy permission default is set for use of the local network.
* `Allow`: The app privacy permission default is set to allow use of the local network.

subkeys.title: Location permission
subkeys.content:
Controls whether an app privacy permission default is set.
* `None`: No app privacy permission default is set for access to location.
* `WhileUsing`: The app privacy permission default is set to allow access to location only while the user is using the app In macOS, this is equivalent to `Always`.
* `Always`: The app privacy permission default is set to allow access to location always.

subkeys.title: Location accuracy permission
subkeys.content:
Controls whether an app privacy permission default is set.
* `None`: No app privacy permission default is set for access to precise location.
* `Approximate`: The app privacy permission default is set to allow approximate access to location.
* `Precise`: The app privacy permission default is set to allow precise access to location.

subkeys.title: Microphone permission
subkeys.content:
Controls whether an app privacy permission default is set.
* `None`: No app privacy permission default is set for use of the microphone.
* `Allow`: The app privacy permission default is set to allow use of the microphone.
